exercise.name: Band Kneeling Single Arm Horizontal Row

reference.title: Band Kneeling Single Arm Horizontal Row
reference.listing: Video (movement reference only; the page could not be fetched from the authoring environment (the proxy refused gymvisual.com), so the data sheet was not read; the movement is taken from the exercise name and standard coaching practice)

breathing.pattern: Breathe out as you row, breathe in as the arm reaches forward again.
breathing.cadence: About 1 s row, short squeeze, about 2 s back

prescription.load: Band tension is user-chosen (bands are colour-coded by tension): pick one you can move for the target reps with 1-3 reps in reserve; step farther from the anchor, or choke up on the band, for more tension.
prescription.progression: More reps, a longer squeeze, kneeling farther from the rack, then the next band up.

cues.text: Tall kneeling facing a rack, knees about hip width, glutes squeezed, trunk tall. The band is looped round the upright at about chest height; hold it in the right hand, arm straight toward the upright, palm facing in. Left hand on the hip.
Breathe out and pull the elbow straight back close to the side until the hand reaches the lower ribs, the shoulder blade drawing back.
Squeeze the shoulder blade toward the spine; hips and shoulders stay square to the rack.
Breathe in and let the arm reach forward again under control, letting the shoulder blade glide forward at the end.
Short pause with the band taut, then row again.

mistakes.mistake: Twisting the trunk to pull the band
mistakes.fix: Keep the hips and shoulders square to the anchor; brace the trunk.
Squeeze the glutes and keep the hips over the knees.
Pull the elbow back and down toward the back pocket.
Keep the elbow close to the side for a horizontal row.

kinematics.norm: Elbow travels straight back close to the side, to a little behind the trunk (clinical opinion)
Nearly straight in front to about 100-120 degrees at the ribs, the forearm staying in line with the band (clinical opinion)
Protracted at the reach, retracted at the end of the row (clinical opinion)
Tall kneeling, hips over the knees: one-arm rows also load the trunk against rotation (Fenwick 2009).
Elastic resistance can give muscle activity comparable to free weights at a matched effort (Andersen 2010).
About 1 s row and 2 s return (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual, Band Kneeling Single Arm Horizontal Row, video (movement reference)
Fenwick, Brown & McGill 2009, comparison of different rowing exercises: trunk muscle activation and lumbar spine motion, load and stiffness (J Strength Cond Res 23(2):350-358)
Lehman et al. 2004, variations in muscle activation levels during traditional latissimus dorsi weight training exercises (Dynamic Medicine 3:4)

Andersen, Andersen, Mortensen, Poulsen, Bjornlund and Zebis 2010, muscle activation and perceived loading during rehabilitation exercises: comparison of dumbbells and elastic resistance (Phys Ther 90(4):538-549)

cautions: Check the band for nicks or tears before every session and replace a worn band; a band that snaps can hit the face or eyes.
Anchor the band to something that cannot move or slip (a rack upright, a pull-up bar or under the feet) and make sure it is secure before loading it.
Band tension rises as it stretches, so the load is heaviest at the end of the pull or push; let it return under control rather than snapping back.
Knee discomfort: kneel on a mat or a folded towel.
Stop if sharp pain, numbness or tingling occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
regressions: Lighter band or kneel closer to the rack.
progressions: Stronger band or kneel farther away.

muscleNotes.lats_r: Extend the shoulder as the elbow drives back (Lehman 2004 compared muscle activity across rows and pulldowns).
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_r: Retract the shoulder blade at the end of the row.
muscleNotes.post_deltoid_r: Extends the arm behind the body.
muscleNotes.infraspinatus_r: Steadies the shoulder through the row.
muscleNotes.upper_traps_r: Steady the shoulder blade; keep it from shrugging.
muscleNotes.core: Braces the trunk in tall kneeling.
muscleNotes.obliques_r: Resist the one-arm pull twisting the trunk (Fenwick 2009 measured trunk muscle demand in rowing exercises).
muscleNotes.obliques_l: Resist the one-arm pull twisting the trunk (Fenwick 2009 measured trunk muscle demand in rowing exercises).
muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Keeps the hips extended over the knees.
muscleNotes.glute_max_l: Keeps the hips extended over the knees.
